source.title: SAUCE: Selective Concept Unlearning in Vision-Language Models with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Qing Li; Jia-Hui Geng; De-Rui Zhu; Feng-Yu Cai; Chenyang Lyu; Fakhri Karray

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendices. Figure 7's plotted values are not available in the text extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether translation and 4-bit quantization affect unlearning in vision-language models, using its own intervention and an unlearning metric.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports unlearning-quality and utility comparisons in Table 2, but those metrics do not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or compare attack recovery with a model that never learned the concept. The robustness results are stated as changes in UAd; the text does not give the figure's individual plotted values or separate the reported drops by attack.
record.test_reason: The study applies two recovery attacks to unlearned vision-language models: Chinese query translation (E) and 4-bit quantization (D). It reports how much unlearning accuracy (UAd) falls for SAUCE and four weight-update baselines (GA, GD, KL, PO). This is a new setting, concept unlearning in VLMs, with a result on whether these attacks recover unlearned concepts and whether the new method (F) resists them.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, with one correction. The authors say all methods lose UAd under the attacks: SAUCE, GA and GD drop 5%, and KL and PO drop over 10%. They call SAUCE 'relatively robust, showing better unlearning quality'. Its advantage in decline is only over KL and PO. Its better post-attack quality largely reflects its higher starting UAd.
record.recipe_differences: SAUCE uses inference-time scaling of selected sparse-autoencoder features in a VLM's vision module, rather than the cited LLM unlearning approaches.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported robustness outcome differs by unlearning method: GA, GD, and SAUCE have a 5% UAd decline, while KL and PO decline by over 10%. The text does not disaggregate outcomes between the two attacks.
record.peer_reviewed: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
record.problems: The robustness outcome is reported through UAd, not a direct measure of recovered knowledge. The text does not report a never-trained control, attack-specific numeric results, uncertainty estimates, or plotted values in the extracted Figure 7.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 unlearning-quality and utility comparisons were not extracted as claim-version rows: they do not measure attack recovery or establish the near-chance targeted-knowledge condition in version A.

untested.parts: The original unlearning methods (RMU, WHP) and near-chance accuracy on knowledge benchmarks are not studied. There is no comparison with a model that never learned the concept.
No fine-tuning or relearning attack is run.
No direction ablation, and no analysis of whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge. SAUCE itself is a feature-suppression method, but its reversibility is not tested.

Only 4-bit quantization is tested, only on LLaVA-v1.5-7B, and only for concrete concepts. The quantization effect is not separated from translation. Llama-3.2-11B-Vision and abstract concepts are not covered, and UAg under attack is not reported.
Only Chinese translation is tested. Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context information are not. The translation effect is not separated from quantization.
SAUCE is not tested against relearning or internal-edit attacks, on the Llama model, or on abstract concepts.

missing.what: Per-attack UAd values (translation alone vs 4-bit quantization alone) and pre- and post-attack values for each method, plotted only in Figure 7

record.verdict_notes: The record's version ids (V1/V2/V5) do not exist; the rows have been relinked to D, E and F. None of the original sources is this study. The attack results come from a single sentence and a figure whose values are not in the text. The text is ambiguous on whether the two attacks were applied jointly or separately, so attack-specific states cannot be determined. The setting differs from the claim's: VLM visual-concept unlearning rather than LLM knowledge unlearning. SAUCE also does not modify weights, which limits how well the quantization test probes D for SAUCE.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not establish near-chance targeted-knowledge accuracy or compare attack recovery with a model that never saw the concept.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery attack is tested.

The study scales selected SAE features to suppress concepts; it does not test whether ablating an activation direction restores them or whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
The paper tests 4-bit quantization on LLaVA-v1.5-7B for concrete concept unlearning, but does not report a never-trained control or establish that most targeted knowledge is recovered.
The tested prompting attack translates queries into Chinese. Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, and in-context information are not tested.
SAUCE is evaluated against Chinese translation and 4-bit quantization on LLaVA-v1.5-7B for concrete concept unlearning; other attacks, models, and tasks are not covered by this robustness experiment.

relation.reason: It reports recovery attacks on unlearned models, though only in one short robustness paragraph.

tranche.reason: New setting (concept unlearning in VLMs) with attack results bearing on D, E and F.

source_check.notes: The only attack evidence is one paragraph plus Figure 7. It gives just the 5% and over-10% declines, with no post-attack values, and its wording doesn't say whether the two attacks were joint or separate. Table 4 confirms SAUCE's pre-attack UAd of 91.5 (LLaVA-v1.5-7B, concrete). The baseline values (60.0/69.2/79.7/84.7) come from the garbled Table 2 and are plausible but can't be firmly placed.

statements.correction: LLaVA-v1.5-7B, concrete concepts: Chinese translation plus 4-bit quantization, reported together. UAd (forget-side accuracy) falls 5% for GA, GD and SAUCE and over 10% for KL and PO. This is partial recovery for every method, so limits_scope on D, not challenges.
statements.problem: The 5-10+% figure and 'not separated' are right. But the study sits under a challenges label, and the statement never says a UAd fall is recovery. All five methods recover partially, which the record's own D verdict (l0) labels limits_scope.

statements.correction: LLaVA-v1.5-7B, concrete concepts: Chinese translation was applied together with 4-bit quantization. UAd fell 5% (GA, SAUCE) and over 10% (KL). The language effect is not isolated, and there is no retrain comparison.
statements.problem: Cites R1, R3 and R5 for a challenges claim (other-language queries stay at or below retrain) but says nothing about this study. Its rows use translation combined with 4-bit quantization and have no retrain comparison. They show partial recovery (the record's E verdict is limits_scope).

statements.correction: R5: SAUCE on LLaVA-v1.5-7B under Chinese translation plus 4-bit quantization (not prompt-only). UAd falls 5% from 91.5%, against over 10% for KL and PO and 5% for GA and GD. The authors call SAUCE 'relatively robust'.
statements.problem: Cites R5 under 'prompt-only attacks without weight access' and a challenges label. R5 combines Chinese translation with 4-bit weight quantization. SAUCE's 5% decline is the record's evidence for F supports (vs KL, PO) and limits_scope (vs GA, GD), not a challenge.
